vague_abstraction.name: Vague abstraction
vague_abstraction.definition: An abstract claim omits the actor, action or comparison a reader needs.
vague_abstraction.useful_when: An abstract summary can help after the concrete mechanism is explained.

unnecessary_jargon.name: Unnecessary jargon
unnecessary_jargon.definition: Specialist or corporate wording adds decoding work without needed precision.
unnecessary_jargon.useful_when: A technical term is useful when the audience needs its exact meaning.

empty_emphasis.name: Empty emphasis
empty_emphasis.definition: Importance, novelty or certainty is asserted without supporting evidence.
empty_emphasis.useful_when: A strong claim can be justified by a named comparison and evidence.

repeated_conclusion.name: Repeated conclusion
repeated_conclusion.definition: A point is restated without new evidence or a useful role in the format.
repeated_conclusion.useful_when: A summary can help in a long report, a slide deck or an accessibility context.

padded_construction.name: Padded construction
padded_construction.definition: Extra scaffolding delays a proposition that could be stated directly.
padded_construction.useful_when: Framing may be needed to distinguish a recommendation from an observed fact.

formulaic_framing.name: Formulaic framing
formulaic_framing.definition: A stock opener, contrast or slogan contributes little to this particular point.
formulaic_framing.useful_when: A familiar structure can orient readers if the content makes it specific.

stacked_hedges.name: Stacked hedges
stacked_hedges.definition: Several uncertainty markers qualify the same claim redundantly.
stacked_hedges.useful_when: Different qualifiers can express different uncertainties, so inspect their scope.

unclear_reference.name: Unclear reference
unclear_reference.definition: The reader cannot recover an actor, pronoun, comparison or logical link.
unclear_reference.useful_when: A pronoun is concise when its referent is clear from the surrounding text.

stock_vocabulary.name: Repeated prestige vocabulary
stock_vocabulary.definition: A small vocabulary of impressive-sounding words recurs across unrelated subjects.
stock_vocabulary.useful_when: Literal or precise use is fine. A model habit requires counts across several topics.
stock_vocabulary.per_post_rule: Does this post use generic prestige diction rather than precise, necessary wording? Cross-topic recurrence is calculated across posts, not inferred from one post.

negative_contrast.name: Unnecessary negative contrast
negative_contrast.definition: A claim is framed by denying an alternative that the reader may never have proposed.
negative_contrast.useful_when: A contrast is useful when correcting an actual misunderstanding.

additive_contrast.name: Automatic not-just expansion
additive_contrast.definition: A simple additional fact is presented as a correction or escalation.
additive_contrast.useful_when: The form can clarify a real limitation in what readers already expect.

triad.name: Mechanical groups of three
triad.definition: Lists or parallel phrases repeatedly use three items regardless of the evidence.
triad.useful_when: Three real findings deserve three items. A triad count cannot decide usefulness.

significance_tail.name: Trailing significance clause
significance_tail.definition: A sentence ends with a participle that announces the importance of the preceding fact.
significance_tail.useful_when: A trailing clause is useful when it states a specific, supported consequence.

inflated_copula.name: Inflated forms of is or has
inflated_copula.definition: A plain relation is replaced by a ceremonial verb phrase.
inflated_copula.useful_when: Serves as is accurate when something has a particular function or role.

question_pivot.name: Question-and-answer pivot
question_pivot.definition: The writer asks a short question and immediately supplies the answer.
question_pivot.useful_when: A question can help when it is the reader's real question and needs explanation.

throat_clearing.name: Throat clearing and signposting
throat_clearing.definition: Text announces the next statement instead of stating it.
throat_clearing.useful_when: Signposts help in a long document when they identify a meaningful change of topic.

vague_attribution.name: Vague attribution
vague_attribution.definition: An opinion or finding is assigned to unnamed authorities.
vague_attribution.useful_when: A collective attribution is useful when its membership and evidence are supplied.

generic_opener.name: Generic scene-setting opener
generic_opener.definition: The first sentence describes a broad era or trend rather than this event.
generic_opener.useful_when: Background can be needed when the intended reader does not know the subject.

engagement_close.name: Generic engagement close
engagement_close.definition: A post ends by soliciting reactions without a specific question grounded in its argument.
engagement_close.useful_when: A focused question can invite useful knowledge that the article does not answer.

formulaic_future.name: Formulaic challenges and future ending
formulaic_future.definition: An ending acknowledges obstacles, then predicts a promising future without specifying either.
formulaic_future.useful_when: Concrete limitations and dated plans are useful, even when placed at the end.

honesty_label.name: Announcing honesty
honesty_label.definition: The writer labels a statement as honest, candid or real rather than supporting it.
honesty_label.useful_when: A candid statement can be appropriate in a personal account; the cue is not proof of insincerity.

payoff.name: Demonstrative payoff sentence
payoff.definition: A paragraph ends with a short this or that sentence that labels its significance.
payoff.useful_when: A short reference can tie together a genuinely complex preceding explanation.

fake_objection.name: Presupposed objection
fake_objection.definition: The writer introduces an imagined reader objection and immediately defeats it.
fake_objection.useful_when: Address an objection when readers have actually raised it or the evidence warrants it.

analyst_metaphor.name: Unexplained analyst metaphor
analyst_metaphor.definition: A figurative word makes a point sound structural, hidden or profound without clarifying it.
analyst_metaphor.useful_when: Literal uses and metaphors with a precise, explained mapping can help.

reflective_pose.name: Staged reflection or discovery
reflective_pose.definition: The writer narrates an insight as a thought that keeps returning or an unexpected discovery.
reflective_pose.useful_when: A true account of reflection is appropriate when the author supplies it.

false_range.name: Decorative or false range
false_range.definition: A from-to construction implies a useful spectrum whose endpoints may not share one scale.
false_range.useful_when: A real range, such as prices from $5 to $20, is informative.

nominalization.name: Noun-heavy wording
nominalization.definition: Actions are packaged as abstract nouns, sometimes hiding who acts.
nominalization.useful_when: Terms such as calibration name useful concepts. A noun suffix does not establish a noun or a defect.

participial_clause.name: Repeated participial clauses
participial_clause.definition: Sentences repeatedly add -ing clauses to compress actions or descriptions.
participial_clause.useful_when: A participial clause is useful when the actor and relationship are clear.

clipped_rhythm.name: Repeated clipped rhythm
clipped_rhythm.definition: Several short sentences or fragments appear consecutively for emphasis.
clipped_rhythm.useful_when: One short sentence can emphasize an important fact; fragments can suit some voices.

bold_density.name: Repeated bold emphasis
bold_density.definition: A post repeatedly applies bold markers to selected phrases.
bold_density.useful_when: A heading or one key figure can benefit from emphasis. LinkedIn may display literal Markdown markers.

bold_leadins.name: Bold labels on every list item
bold_leadins.definition: List entries repeatedly begin with a bold label and a colon.
bold_leadins.useful_when: Consistent labels are useful when comparing genuinely parallel attributes.

emoji_layout.name: Emoji as repeated layout markers
emoji_layout.definition: Emoji introduce many lines, headings or bullet-like statements.
emoji_layout.useful_when: Emoji may fit an author's voice or aid scanning. Their presence is not inherently poor writing.

title_case.name: Title case and heading templates
title_case.definition: Short posts use formal, capitalized section headings or repeat the same heading scheme.
title_case.useful_when: Headings help in long or complex posts and may follow a publication's house style.
title_case.per_post_rule: Does this post use a formal title-case heading or a repeated generic heading template? Proper nouns alone do not qualify.

single_sentence_paragraphs.name: Mechanical one-sentence paragraphs
single_sentence_paragraphs.definition: Most paragraphs contain one sentence, repeatedly separated by blank lines.
single_sentence_paragraphs.useful_when: Short paragraphs can improve mobile reading. Density and runs are descriptive, not quality thresholds.
single_sentence_paragraphs.per_post_rule: Does the post repeatedly isolate single sentences as paragraphs? Treat this as a visible structure, not proof that readers dislike it.

markup_residue.name: Chatbot or markup residue
markup_residue.definition: The response includes assistant-facing commentary, placeholders or formatting artifacts instead of only the finished post.
markup_residue.useful_when: An explicit placeholder may be useful in a requested template, and an editorial note can prevent an error.

invented_experience.name: Unsupported first-person experience
invented_experience.definition: The draft gives the poster a personal experience, observation or emotion that the supplied material does not establish.
invented_experience.useful_when: First-person judgment is different from biography. An author-supplied experience is valid.
invented_experience.per_post_rule: Is a personal experience attributed to the intended poster without support in the supplied article or author context? First-person analysis alone is not personal experience. The prompt supplied no biography.

generic_benefit.name: Generic benefit language
generic_benefit.definition: A product benefit is described without saying what task changes or for whom.
generic_benefit.useful_when: A short slogan can accompany a specific explanation, especially in advertising.

uniform_rhythm.name: Uniform sentence and paragraph rhythm
uniform_rhythm.definition: Successive sentences or paragraphs repeatedly have the same length or internal template.
uniform_rhythm.useful_when: Parallel structure can help readers compare genuinely similar cases.

punctuation_tics.name: Repeated punctuation for emphasis
punctuation_tics.definition: One punctuation device repeatedly supplies pauses, suspense or excitement.
punctuation_tics.useful_when: Punctuation can convey a real relationship or fit an author's voice. Count it without treating it as proof of AI authorship.

hashtag_tail.name: Automatic hashtag tail
hashtag_tail.definition: Every post ends with a block of generic topic labels.
hashtag_tail.useful_when: A relevant tag can help organize a series or address a particular community.
hashtag_tail.per_post_rule: Does this post end in a generic hashtag block? Do not infer automatic use in other posts.

reasoning_effort: Not exposed by the Decisions endpoint; no unsupported effort parameter. Original four writers remain high.
tools: No tools/search offered; all evidence supplied in state.
blinding: Writer identity and conversation history withheld; post and source article supplied.
labels: 40 independent Bernoulli probabilities in each zone; labels overlap and need not sum to one.
ambiguous_band: 0.2 < p < 0.8; retained rather than manually resolved.
unit: article clusters; 2000 article bootstrap draws; turn and family member counts retained.
smoke: Two fixed saved posts, both batches; no tuning to returned labels. Main reuses identical smoke requests.
failures: One attempt per exact request, all raw responses saved. Refusals/missing/invalid probabilities remain unreadable, not absent.
cache: Cache every response by full-payload hash. Keep article/post/pattern definitions stable between two batches. Record native cache fields if exposed; do not infer missing counters as zero.
rights: Complete wire bodies local/git-ignored; public request hashes and typed responses retained.
evidence_limit: Classifier opinions, not human-validated defects or a factual accuracy score. Earlier regex/layout outputs are diagnostics, not assigned labels.
